source_snapshot.procedure: Cause an event/error/alert, verify it in management or OS logs, confirm the corresponding Logs Callout record, and check configured notification methods such as email or SMS.
source_snapshot.criteria: All call out way can get pass result.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek proposes changing SEL time and sending predefined `ipmitool event 1`, then reading SEL and LAN alert configuration. This changes chronology, does not prove the event is source-appropriate and does not prove delivery to every required receiver.

original_test_intent.purpose: Validate the complete event-to-callout chain for every notification method required by the platform recipe: an approved representative event is logged, mapped to the correct callout, delivered to the intended test receiver, and contains the required identity, severity, code and timestamp fields.
original_test_intent.target: The exact BMC/management alert policy, its required callout transports and isolated test destinations/receivers, plus the corresponding BMC/OS event and callout logs.
original_test_intent.scope: Freeze the required callout-method matrix and event-to-policy mapping; preserve clocks, SEL and logs; safely trigger each approved event needed to exercise the matrix; verify local logging, callout creation, outbound attempt and receiver-side delivery for every required method; then restore any temporary test configuration and prove no residual alert storm.
original_test_intent.operation: Record BMC identity, synchronized time sources, alert policy and receiver baselines; obtain approval for a reversible platform-specific stimulus; arm isolated receivers; trigger the event without changing SEL time; correlate the new source event, BMC callout record and each required receiver receipt by event identity and timestamps; observe retry/timeout behavior if specified; restore temporary destinations and retain evidence.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: At least one independently traceable delivery observation for every required callout method and event-policy row in the owner-supplied matrix. The 20-minute attended and 10-minute machine fields are estimates, not permission to omit a method or shorten documented delivery/retry timeout.
original_test_intent.expected_result: The approved event appears exactly as specified in the source log and callout record; every required callout method reaches only its intended isolated receiver within the specified timeout/retry policy with correct fields; no unrequested recipient, duplicate storm, clock corruption or platform impact occurs; cleanup and final health succeed.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Signed callout-method/event-policy/receiver matrix; BMC identity/firmware and time-sync state; redacted alert configuration; preserved pre-event logs; exact stimulus and approval; new SEL/BMC/OS callout record; outbound status; per-method receiver-side message/log and correlation; retry/timeout results; cleanup and final health.
ambiguities: `All call out way` does not enumerate which transports or destinations are mandatory for this platform.
The source gives event examples but no exact safe event, severity, expected message schema, retry interval or delivery timeout.
It is unclear whether one event must fan out to all methods or whether separate event-policy rows must be exercised.
The DeepSeek command changes SEL time and only inspects configuration, neither of which proves receiver delivery.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly rejects the SEL-time change and blind `event 1`, requires reversible stimulus, isolated receivers, receiver-side evidence and rollback, and preserves the classification. However, its purpose and command reduce the source's `all call out way` criterion to one event through a singular approved destination, allowing untested required notification methods.

applicable_history.decision: The historical PARTIAL record accepts the DeepSeek command direction but does not prove receiver delivery or define the all-method scope.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Keep the automation class but rewrite V2's reduced one-destination scope. The test must cover every callout method required by the platform's signed matrix with receiver-side delivery evidence; no stimulus is allowed until that matrix, a reversible event and isolated destinations are approved.

available_now: BMC identity, firmware, current time synchronization, alert policy metadata and existing SEL/callout logs can be collected read-only without changing chronology.
The source clearly requires source logging, a corresponding callout record and notification-method validation, not merely event injection.
Upstream ipmitool identifies `event 1` as a predefined Temperature Upper Critical test event and implements SEL time setting as a write; neither is a generic read-only baseline action.
missing_inputs: Authoritative list of every required callout method, destination/receiver, event-policy row, message fields, severity, timeout, retry and duplicate-suppression rule
Exact platform-qualified reversible stimulus for each required policy path, including whether one fan-out event or multiple events are required
Isolated receiver endpoints and access to receiver-side logs with protected credentials/certificates/secrets and redaction policy
BMC/OS/receiver clock-correlation tolerance, alert-config backup/restore, rate limit, cleanup, OOB recovery and maintenance approval
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The BMC/platform owner supplies event-policy and callout-method requirements; messaging/network/security owners supply isolated receivers and delivery criteria; the lab owner approves stimulus, rate limits, cleanup and recovery.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Export BMC/firmware identity, SEL time and time-sync status, alert/callout policy metadata, receiver inventory and preserved current logs without clearing or setting them.
Validate log collection and receiver-side evidence access using existing benign records, while marking delivery capability untested.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not change SEL time, clear logs, send `ipmitool event 1` blindly, simulate hardware/network/storage failure, change production notification settings or contact production recipients.
Do not infer delivery from configured destinations, a local SEL entry or an outbound attempt; do not declare PASS until every required method has a correlated receiver receipt.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The signed matrix enumerates all methods and policy rows; every stimulus is reversible and maps to an expected message; isolated receivers and clocks are ready; rate limits, approvals, rollback and OOB recovery are verified; a dry run proves evidence correlation without contacting production.

revision_candidate.test_name: BMC Callout Delivery Across All Required Notification Methods
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify that an approved BMC event is logged and delivered through every callout method required by the platform recipe, with end-to-end event and receiver correlation.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The exact BMC/firmware and approved alert-policy recipe, connected only to isolated test receivers for every required notification transport, with synchronized clocks, protected secrets and OOB recovery.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Every method and event-policy row in the signed platform callout matrix; an unlisted example such as email or SMS is not automatically applicable, and a single successful destination cannot stand in for other required methods.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Callout-method/event-policy/receiver matrix; safe reversible stimuli; expected event identity/severity/code/message fields; receiver endpoints and security materials; timeout/retry/deduplication limits; clock tolerance; package/vendor commands; approvals; config backup, cleanup and recovery plan.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Preserve configuration, clocks, SEL and receiver baselines. For each matrix row, arm the isolated receiver, trigger only the approved reversible event, capture the new source event and BMC callout record, then prove receiver-side delivery and required fields within the specified timeout/retry policy. Correlate by identity and timestamps, prevent uncontrolled repeats, restore temporary settings and verify final health.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Correct BMC and firmware identified; all required methods enumerated; isolated non-production receivers reachable; time sources synchronized; secrets protected; event mapping and reversible stimuli validated; log capacity, rate limits, backup/rollback, OOB recovery, maintenance window and explicit approval available.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Signed matrix and redacted alert policy; time-sync baseline; exact stimulus/approval; pre/post SEL and BMC/OS callout logs; per-method outbound status and receiver receipt/message with identity, severity, code and timestamps; timeout/retry/deduplication observations; restored configuration and no residual alerts.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The exact platform BMC alert/callout specification and approved notification-service policy; upstream ipmitool defines test-event mechanics but does not define platform routing or delivery acceptance.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never alter SEL time or clear evidence, inject an unvalidated event, trigger real hardware/service faults without separate approval, send to production recipients, expose secrets, exceed rate limits or treat configuration/SEL presence as proof of receiver delivery.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: BMC, notification-service, network/security and lab owners approve the matrix, stimuli, test receivers, rate limits, impact, rollback and cleanup before any event is generated.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Owners select applicable methods and safe events and judge any external provider behavior. After approval, the agent can trigger supported stimuli, collect logs/receipts, correlate the end-to-end chain, enforce timeouts and package evidence.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On wrong recipient/event, alert storm, credential exposure, BMC/network/host impact or failed cleanup, stop stimuli, preserve all logs, disable only the approved temporary test path, restore the backed-up policy, revoke exposed secrets if needed, verify BMC/OOB and receiver health, and require owner disposition before retry.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Incomplete method matrix, unsafe/ambiguous stimulus, production destination, unavailable receiver evidence, clock mismatch beyond tolerance, wrong or duplicate notification, rate-limit breach, missing event-to-receipt correlation, BMC/OOB loss, platform impact or failed rollback/cleanup.

identified_defects: V2 narrows the source's all-callout-method acceptance to one approved destination.
DeepSeek changes SEL chronology and uses a fixed event whose semantics may not match the platform policy under test.
Configuration and source-side logs alone cannot prove end-to-end notification delivery.
reason_for_change: Restore the original all-method acceptance scope and make receiver-side delivery, per-method correlation and retry/timeout behavior mandatory while retaining V2's safe-event, isolated-destination and no-clock-change controls.

new_technical_evidence.title: ipmitool README
new_technical_evidence.version: upstream master accessed 2026-10-13; installed version must be recorded
new_technical_evidence.applicability: BMCs accepting standard ipmitool test-event commands
new_technical_evidence.supports: `ipmitool event 1` is specifically a Temperature Upper Critical Going High test event, not a platform-neutral placeholder for any callout policy.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Whether this BMC routes that synthetic event through every required callout path is platform-specific.

new_technical_evidence.title: ipmitool SEL command definitions
new_technical_evidence.supports: GET SEL Time and SET SEL Time are distinct commands; setting a fixed SEL time is a state change and must not be used as a harmless baseline step.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Platform time synchronization and rollback behavior remain vendor-specific.

removed_ambiguities: Defines `all call out way` through an owner-signed method/policy matrix rather than a singular destination.
Requires receiver-side proof and separates it from local event/callout logging.
Makes one-event fan-out versus multiple-event coverage an explicit engineering input.
resolved_blockers: Read-only inventory and log preservation can proceed now; a deterministic hybrid test is technically executable once the platform callout matrix, stimuli and isolated receivers are supplied.
remaining_blockers: No event generation until all required methods, event mappings, safe stimuli, isolated receivers, timing/rate limits, approvals and rollback are resolved.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 prevents a false completion after one destination by restoring every required callout path, adds receiver-side delivery proof and policy-row traceability, and keeps V2's prohibition on SEL-time mutation, blind event injection and production recipients.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The restored all-method scope and high-risk event/callout contract are queued for isolated validation.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source requires event logging, a Logs Callout record and notification-method checks, while its criterion explicitly says all callout ways must pass.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 corrects the unsafe DeepSeek commands but reduces all required callout ways to one event and one destination.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Preserve clocks/logs, require a safe event and isolated receivers, and accept only correlated source/callout/receiver evidence for every signed method.
